design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing - she would like to pay in the next lot of subsidy money - and the size of that lot cannot be read off anything. It is the cover period's expected need less the share of the funding still drawable, and the funding still drawable is wrong at the opening in two ways she never mentions: the settlement for the months the market has stood shut has never been raised, and the balance left in the funding lots that ran past their drawable life has never been handed back. Both are problems with their own multi-factor computation over the ledger and the service request log, and the second is measured against the first. The customer knows none of it; every hop has to come out of the published rules.

SCOPE CLAIMED AND HEADROOM. Task 0 occupied the catch-up drawdown, the product settlement true-up, the outage service credit and the settlement payment, with their four tools. This task claims the three reserved for it: market_ext_standby_period_settlement, market_ext_lapsed_lot_settlement_credit and market_ext_subsidy_funding_lot, with post_market_standby_settlement_ab27821d, issue_lapsed_funding_credit_131d77d2 and fund_market_subsidy_lot_f6d53aaa. The two tasks share no policy and no tool and between them cover every extended policy of the difficulty.

THE STEP 0 DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0013_workplace_dining_and_catering_provider/tasks/micro_market_desk --task 1): {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 5]}. market_ext_standby_period_settlement took the count of 4; market_ext_lapsed_lot_settlement_credit and market_ext_subsidy_funding_lot took 5.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root problem: market_ext_subsidy_funding_lot. Edges, both value_input:
  (a) market_ext_lapsed_lot_settlement_credit <- market_ext_standby_period_settlement. gate: settlement_base. form: state. prerequisite sentence in market_ext_lapsed_lot_settlement_credit's own rule: 'The credit handed back for a lapsed funding lot is fixed only after the monthly settlement charge for the period the market stood shut stands on the agreement.' Four-point test: the connective is 'only after'; the waited-on side is a record-visible state - a monthly settlement charge raised for the shut period, in the words the ledger uses; no tool, policy id or code token; the strength is hard and the scope is exactly that charge. Contrapositive: 'the credit handed back for a lapsed funding lot is not fixed before the monthly settlement charge for the period the market stood shut stands on the agreement.' Exactly one write of this difficulty brings it about: post_market_standby_settlement_ab27821d; the product settlement claimed by task 0 is raised for a period the kiosk was trading, and its own rule says no product settlement is raised for a period the market stood shut. Unresolved at the opening: the last monthly settlement charge on the ledger is the July management line raised 2026-08-18 for the period 2026-07, and the only row on the open invoice INV-MK-451702 is a restocking charge, which is not a monthly settlement charge; the condition is now written to that narrower state, which is what it always meant. Deletion sensitivity (actual run): with the standing charge, the credit computes 1249.22; skipping it, 755.00, because the period ceiling then bites.
  (b) market_ext_subsidy_funding_lot <- market_ext_lapsed_lot_settlement_credit. gate: drawable_balance. form: state. sentence in market_ext_subsidy_funding_lot's own rule: 'The lot the client pays in is not fixed before a service credit naming no kiosk stands on the agreement, being the funding handed back to the client on a settlement.' The state is record-visible because the two crediting tools of this difficulty write different rows: the outage credit stamps the posting with the agreement's kiosk and this one leaves the kiosk reference empty, which both rules state. Exactly one write produces a service credit naming no kiosk: issue_lapsed_funding_credit_131d77d2. Unresolved at the opening: no service credit of any kind stands on this agreement's ledger. Deletion sensitivity: with the credit, the lot computes 19462.41; skipping it, 18837.80.
Topological order: market_ext_standby_period_settlement -> market_ext_lapsed_lot_settlement_credit -> market_ext_subsidy_funding_lot, a chain that admits exactly one linear order; there are no parallel prerequisites and so no second terminal state. user_scenario names neither prerequisite problem nor the acts they perform. The tool layer validates no prerequisite: all three functions perform one ctx.create and one ctx.update carrying that posting's own account delta, with no branch on a preceding row.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Step 8 writes market_monthly_settlement_invoiced, governed by market_settlement_terms (settlement_state: installing, active or suspended - suspended here, which is exactly the state the standing charge is written for), and by market_agg_portfolio_settlement_band and market_combination_dining_interaction, neither of which carries structured eligibility for that subject, so both are inherited as policy_scope; the band's own discount clause is superseded by a declared overwrite on market_ext_standby_period_settlement, since a settlement raised for a shut period takes no portfolio discount. Step 10 writes market_service_credit_issued, governed by market_service_credit_terms, whose gate credit_claim_window is a time gate: anchor 'the day the settlement invoice was posted', anchor source market_ledger.posted_date, relation not_after, duration variants.service_credit_claim_window_days (21 for Smart Store Micro Market), calendar days from the day after the posting day, boundary inclusive. INV-MK-451702 was posted 2026-09-18, so the window closes at the end of 2026-10-09; frozen_time is 2026-09-22, four days in. Boundary cases: a claim on 2026-10-09 is the last day still in time; on 2026-10-10 it is out of time. Step 12 writes market_subsidy_funding_posted, governed by market_subsidy_funding_terms (fundable_state: installing, active or suspended - suspended here, which base expressly permits). Smart Store's subsidy model is percent_discount, so the format takes funding at all. The base lot-expiry sentence of market_subsidy_funding_terms is inherited unchanged and is what market_ext_lapsed_lot_settlement_credit's own lapse window now implements, which is why that policy cites it in base_policy_refs.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The target objects are the open September settlement invoice INV-MK-451702 on the micro market agreement at site CS-462, kiosk MK-44207, and the agreement's funding record. The correlation key for the standing charge and the credit is that invoice reference; for the lot it is the agreement. Rows excluded and why: the lots of 2026-02-10 and 2026-07-08 fall inside the twelve months a Smart Store lot stays drawable and are therefore not lapsed - they are the near-miss for the lapse window; the ten drawdown postings inside those twelve months are not set against the lapsed funding; the equipment and settlement charges of 2026-06-18 and 2026-07-18 fall outside the two months the settlement is read over. Already settled: each of the three earlier invoices carries a payment for its exact total of 2855.00, so what stands unsettled is the September restocking line of 165.00 and the disputed shrink adjustment of 742.50, which is receivable_balance_usd 907.50 exactly.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS. The four funding lots and the twenty-six drawdown postings carry the lapse window, the drawdown attribution, the cover period, the take-up and the handling step; subsidy_pool_balance_usd of 6780.00 is exactly 27,000.00 funded less 20,220.00 drawn. Each drawdown row is a kiosk day settlement carrying the day reference it was settled under, and every one is far inside a day's ceiling for the site - 480 badged staff at the 9.00 per employee per day printed against the format, and a largest row of 830.00. The seven settlement charges and three payments carry the standing-charge rate, the lapsed-credit share and the settlement-reading window. The single shrink adjustment puts the funding lot on the low contingency. The twelve service requests carry the closure months, the held-over planogram step, the closure relief and the lapse share, and the declined claim and the planogram request still in the received state are the near-misses a careless reader counts as approved. The cafe contract and its six ledger rows carry the cross-difficulty factor: 16,070.00 of client subsidy met at the cafe over the trailing year puts the management fee on the pooled share. Automatic clauses checked: the closure has run 39 days against a 45-day contract-year ceiling, so base's reopen-or-give-notice obligation has not fallen due; no invoice is past due beyond its grace days; the credit hold threshold of 75 days past due is not approached; both quantity fields reconcile exactly with the event stream and are maintained by every write.

PERSONA DESIGN. Harriet is careful and a little anxious, reads figures off paper rather than summarising, and explains the refurbishment before she gets to the point - a different voice from task 0's brisk accounts-payable caller. She volunteers the refurbishment, the wish to pay in the next lot and her insistence on moving the money herself; everything else comes only when asked. She cannot say what is left in the pot and says so. Her passive reactions hang on things the agent says, and her last reaction answers the last gold action and stops.

THE PREREQUISITE CHAIN, DEPTH AND BREADTH. The lot rule waits on a service credit naming no kiosk standing on the agreement; the credit rule waits on the monthly settlement charge for the shut period. So a request to pay money in walks back to a settlement that was never raised. Breadth: the lot reads the funding lots, the drawdown history over two windows, the credits, the suspension requests, the shrink adjustments and the format's drawable life and product count; the credit reads the funding and drawdown history against the format's own drawable life, the settlement charges over three windows, the payment history, the outage, resumption and planogram requests; the standing charge reads the suspension start date, the suspension requests, the payment history, the planogram and resumption requests and the client's cafe contract and cafe ledger. Removing either edge changes a scored number (755.00 against 1249.22; 18837.80 against 19462.41).

EASY MISTAKES AND HOW POLICY EXCLUDES THEM. Treating every lot as lapsed, when the rule dates the lapse from the months the format itself keeps a lot drawable - twelve for Smart Store - so the 2026-02-10 and 2026-07-08 lots are still live. Setting every drawdown against the lapsed funding rather than only what was drawn before those twelve months. Rounding the 39 closed days down to one month instead of up to two. Charging the management fee in full when the cafe at the site carries the programme. Reading the settlement over the month alone rather than the two months the format's invoice day puts it on. Setting the whole drawable balance against the cover need instead of half. Forgetting that the credit the desk has just allowed is itself taken off the drawable balance. Counting the restocking charge on the open invoice as the settlement the credit waits for.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate the profile by the organisation name, verify on the account code and the billing postcode, read the agreement, its ledger, its service request log, the cafe contract and the cafe ledger. Then: (1) raise the standing charge of 2633.70 for the closure on INV-MK-451702; (2) allow the lapsed funding credit of 1249.22 against the same invoice; (3) unlock the funding tool, hand it to the customer, and have her pay in 19462.41 by ach.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The three computations were replayed against the seed with the real tools at their own handling times: 2633.70, 1249.22 and 19462.41, equal to computations[].expected and to the gold arguments. Per-factor baseline substitution moved the result in all fourteen cases; substituting every factor's baseline at once gave 1920.00, 0.00 and 2969.22, each different from gold. Skipping each prerequisite write gave 755.00 and 18837.80. Zeroing the history aggregates and forcing the cross-category reads off both moved the results. Every intermediate figure quoted in factor_trace and in argument_uniqueness_tracing was taken from a binding-by-binding dump of the same replay rather than written by hand.

CLOSURE. market_ext_standby_period_settlement -> post_market_standby_settlement_ab27821d -> step 8 -> the standing charge on INV-MK-451702; market_ext_lapsed_lot_settlement_credit -> issue_lapsed_funding_credit_131d77d2 -> step 10 -> the credit against the same invoice; market_ext_subsidy_funding_lot -> fund_market_subsidy_lot_f6d53aaa -> step 12 -> the funding lot on the agreement. charter_scope.extended_policies equals the set of computations.policy_id equals the problems of the tree, and required_documents repeats it verbatim in order. Across the difficulty the two tasks' scopes are disjoint and together cover all seven extended policies. After the three writes subsidy_pool_balance_usd reads 26242.41 and receivable_balance_usd 2291.98, each tool having carried its own posting's account delta.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected and this dossier masked: the request is to pay in the next lot; the lot rule's waiting condition is visibly unmet because no credit stands on the ledger; the credit rule's waiting condition is visibly unmet because no monthly settlement charge has been raised for the closure; so the order is forced and the three figures come out at 2633.70, 1249.22 and 19462.41, matching gold.

REVISION 2 - the round-1 policy-task audit, item by item.
  C-2 / F-1-3 (RED, undeclared override of the base lot-expiry rule, leaving 1329.22 against 669.22 and 8548.51 against 8218.51): routed around rather than declared, which removes the divergence instead of licensing it. market_ext_lapsed_lot_settlement_credit no longer invents a six-month lapse window; its rule now says a lot stays drawable for the months printed against the market format, counted from the day the funding cleared, and the compute implements exactly that with a fork on the format's own subsidy_funding_lot_expiry_months (6, 9 or 12 across the six formats). Base and extended now give the same answer to 'has this lot lapsed?', so no overwrite is needed; market_subsidy_funding_terms has nevertheless been added to base_policy_refs, because it is now genuine input lineage. why_false no longer asserts one reading while the gold uses another: it names the two lots, cleared 2025-03-12 and 2025-06-18, that the base rule itself makes lapsed, and the gold value 13,000.00 is exactly their sum.
  C-13 / F-1-1 (RED, three ladders with an unreachable tier): long_drawable_life_months is now 12, not 18, so 'at or beyond the long drawable life' is true of the four formats that keep a lot drawable for twelve months and false of the two that keep it for six and nine - both sides live, and this agreement sits on the first. The ladder that used the parameter inside market_ext_lapsed_lot_settlement_credit is gone altogether, replaced by settlement_reading_window, whose tiers fork on the format's invoice cycle day (5, 8, 10, 12, 15, 18 across the six formats) and so divide real customers. The kiosk_handling_step ladder no longer turns on the mobile wallet, which every fundable format carries; it turns on the format's distinct product count against the wide-range count of 250, which splits the six formats 60/140/280/420/650/380. No factor's declared baseline now sits on a tier no customer can reach.
  F-1-8 (a stated baseline figure of 5,800.00 that failed recomputation): the ladder that sentence belonged to no longer exists, and every figure in this task's factor_trace is now taken from a machine dump of each binding at its own handling time rather than written by hand; the same sweep was applied to task 0.
  C-5 (rule said 'rounded half up' while the evaluator rounds half to even, live on the 1413.425 period ceiling): every rule, baseline, basis and docstring now states the convention the code applies, so the ceiling is 1413.42 in both the prose and the binding.
  C-7 / F-1-2 (the edge condition was broader than its sentence, and the restocking charge satisfied it literally): the sentence and the condition now both say 'monthly settlement charge', which the restocking line is not, and why_false says so explicitly.
  C-8 (credits_all counted credits that are not funding handed back): the binding now filters on an empty kiosk reference, which is exactly the record mark that separates a funding hand-back from a credit answering kiosk hours, and the rule sentence it quotes says so.
  C-12 (the portfolio band was never applied): declared as an overwrite on market_agg_portfolio_settlement_band in market_ext_standby_period_settlement, quoting the base clause and replacing it with the sentence that no portfolio discount is taken off a settlement raised for a shut period.
  C-3 / F-0-4 (docstrings asserted balance effects the code never performed): every tool now carries its posting's account delta to the agreement's quantity field.
  C-6 (an ordering word in the docstrings): removed.
  F-1-4 (the lot's service_period was not uniquely fixed): the tool schema now pins it to the period the lot clears in, which frozen_time settles.
  F-1-5 (drawdown rows against the per-purchase grain and the daily cap): the size contradiction is closed - each row is a kiosk day settlement for the whole site, carrying a kiosk day reference, and 830.00 at most against a site day ceiling of 4320.00. The residual is accepted and recorded: the base event's grain line reads one row per purchase, and db_schema.json and the product charter are frozen blueprint; seeding a real month of per-purchase rows would be thousands of rows and no relationship of this task turns on the grain, every binding reading the rows as sums or counts.
  F-1-6 (the suspension had passed the base annual ceiling with nothing to do about it): the closure now starts 2026-08-14 and has run 39 days at frozen_time, inside the 45-day contract-year ceiling printed against the format, so no obligation base creates is left unanswered. The closure months still round up to 2, so no factor lost its tier.
  F-1-7 (three figures in play for 'the money left in the pot'): the pool the agreement records is 6780.00, the funding still drawable 6200.00 before the credit and 4950.78 after it, and the balance left unspent in the lapsed lots 580.00 - each named after what it is by the sentence that uses it, and the credit handed back is now comfortably smaller than the pool rather than larger than it.


REVISION 3 - the round-2 policy-task audit, item by item.
  R-2 (the seeded drawdown ledger against the declared grain, and four ladders forking on counts of those rows): the second half is closed outright and the first is recorded with its arithmetic. Closed: no ladder in this difficulty now forks on a count of these rows. drawdown_attribution_basis forks on the amount drawn against the agreement rather than on the number of postings; take_up_share and kiosk_handling_step fork on the amount drawn at the kiosk over the trailing year rather than on a posting count. The three parameters that carried those counts are gone and are replaced by amount floors, and the tiers this world sits on are unchanged, so gold, every whole baseline, every sensitivity and both skip figures are identical before and after - verified by re-derivation, not assumed. The remaining count forks in the charter are of funding lots, service requests, settlement charges, payments, credits and disputes, each of which is one row per business object by its own event's grain.
  Recorded rather than fixed: the rows themselves are still kiosk day settlements, not the single purchases the base event's grain declares. The reason is arithmetic, not the frozen base line. The credit this task computes hands back the unspent balance of a lapsed funding lot, and a lot may not be smaller than the 6500.00 minimum printed against Smart Store Micro Market - the smallest minimum on any format that carries a management fee at all. For the credit to be anything but the whole lot, the lot must be nearly consumed, which on a per-purchase ledger at the 9.00 per employee per day ceiling is of the order of a thousand rows. Left unconsumed, the credit would be about 6500.00 against a period ceiling of a quarter of a monthly settlement, some 1400.00, so the ceiling would bite and every factor beneath it would stop bearing weight. The day-settlement shape is what makes this computation expressible in a world that is also the task's whole database; each row is well inside a day's ceiling for the site, 480 badged staff against the 9.00 per employee per day printed against the format, with a largest row of 830.00.
  R-4 (a claim about the rework that did not hold): corrected. Round 2 was reported as having moved gold on every computation of both tasks. market_ext_standby_period_settlement did not move: it is 2633.70 in round 1, round 2 and round 3, with baseline_result 1920.00 and sensitivities 1358.10 / 2746.50 / 3809.70 / 2551.20 unchanged throughout. Shortening the closure from 57 to 39 calendar days left ceil(39/30) = ceil(57/30) = 2 whole months, and no other input of that computation moved. The figure is right for the world it is computed on; only the claim was wrong.
  F-0-9 / R-3 (a proof face left behind on task 0): the fix is described in task 0's dossier. It reaches this task too: every proof face here - both why_false blocks, both flips_to_true_by blocks, both edge_load_bearing entries and the agreement's seed_consistency check - is now generated by interpolation from the same machine fact pack rather than written by hand, and the strict verifier that reports every number a face states which the machine run does not produce reports none on this task outside the revision log.
  C-6 and C-10 / R-1: both closed in the charter and the tool module; see task 0's dossier. Neither bears on this task's world.
user_scenario:
Harriet Rothwell handles facilities and workplace services for Tessaly Precision Works at their Detroit plant, and the smart-store micro market in the canteen corridor sits under her budget. The floor it stands on has been closed off since the middle of August for a refurbishment, and the builders have told her the corridor will be handed back within the fortnight. She is a careful, slightly anxious caller who reads things out rather than summarising them, and she explains the refurbishment before she gets to the point.

What she wants is straightforward: she would like to pay in the next lot of subsidy money so that the discount is sitting there for staff the day the market reopens, and she says the finance committee has signed off whatever the desk works out as the right size of lot. She is clear that she would rather move the money herself out of their own payables run than have anyone at Larkspur Table take it, and she says she will do it by bank transfer the moment she is told the amount and given the screen for it.

She reads the client account code off the last invoice, CA-44318, and if the agent wants another detail she reads the billing postcode from the same sheet, 48226. She will give her direct line, 5035274618, if a third thing is wanted, and she gives her name, Harriet Rothwell, when she is asked who is calling. Asked which market it is she says the one at the Detroit plant, in the canteen corridor, and she apologises for not knowing any reference for it. If the agent asks whether there is a purchase order, she says everything for that site goes on PO-TS-2026-407.

She has no idea how much is left in the subsidy pot and says so; she can see a figure on the portal but does not know what it means and would rather be told. She does not know what the market costs while it is shut either, and if the agent quotes her any figure she writes it down without arguing. If the agent tells her there is something to be put straight on the account before the lot can be sized, she says of course, go ahead, and does not ask what it is. Whenever the agent tells her a charge or a credit has gone on the account she says thank you and waits.

When the agent has unlocked the payment screen for her and told her the amount, she pays it in herself there and then by bank transfer, and she reads the confirmation back off her screen. Once the desk tells her the lot is on the agreement she thanks them, says she will let the staff know, and rings off.

request_binding.action_semantics: The agreement has stood suspended since 2026-08-14 and no settlement has been raised for any part of that closure, so the standing charge the format owes for a shut market is outstanding on the record; that selects a monthly settlement charge rather than a credit or a funding posting.

discriminator.business_meaning: the standing charge owed for the months the market has stood shut

stage_provenance.fact: The standing charge for the closure is invoiced to the client at the moment this charge is raised.

base_preconditions.condition: The settlement a client pays on each micro market is discounted by a portfolio band read across its whole market estate; the client holds one micro market, so the ladder sits on its lowest step and discounts nothing, and the policy sets no gate on raising the charge.

A settlement is only invoiced while the agreement stands installing, active or suspended; a suspended market is invoiced the standby charge printed against its format in place of the equipment lease, and no product settlement is raised at all.

What the client holds elsewhere in the dining programme changes what the market settles; the cafe contract at the site is read only for the share of the management fee carried during the closure, and the policy sets no gate on raising a settlement charge.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the client organisation profile the caller speaks for, so the rest of the call has a profile reference to work from.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Without the profile reference nothing else on this client can be retrieved and identity cannot be checked.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record a passing identity check on the profile against two details the caller reads off her last invoice.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing may be quoted back about the account, and no money may be moved on it, until this has passed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull the client's micro market agreements: the format held, that the agreement stands suspended, the day the closure began, the site and kiosk, the badged headcount, the unspent subsidy funding and the unsettled balance.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The format fixes every printed parameter of the three calculations; the suspension start date fixes the closed days; the badged headcount drives the expected need; the unsettled balance decides the standing-charge rate.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull the whole settlement ledger: the three funding lots with their clearing dates, every kiosk drawdown, the settlement charges and the invoice they sit on, the payments and the shrink adjustment.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The lapsed funding, the drawdowns set against it, the settlement the credit is measured over, the payment history behind two share tiers and the drawable balance behind the lot are all reconciled from these rows.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull the service request log: the approved suspension and resumption requests, the approved planogram changes, the approved and declined kiosk outage requests and the planogram request still in the received state.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The closure months, the held-over planogram step, the closure relief, the lapse share, the take-up, the contingency and the drawable offset all rest on these rows.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the client's workplace cafe contract at the same site: the service model held and whether it stands active.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The management fee share factor turns on whether a cafe contract for the client stands active while the market is shut.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the cafe ledger: the client subsidy met at the cafe over the trailing year.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The management fee share tier turns on how much client subsidy the cafe has met over the twelve months, which decides what share of the market management fee is charged during the closure.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden write that invoices the standing charge a micro market carries while it is closed off.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it changes nothing in the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Raise the standing charge the agreement owes for the months the market has stood shut on the open settlement invoice.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: market_ext_standby_period_settlement is the only policy that computes standby_settlement_usd, and the lapsed funding credit waits on this charge standing on the agreement.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.market_agreement_id: Value: the micro market agreement row id returned by find_market_agreements. Basis: the tool schema says 'the reference number identifying the micro market agreement being invoiced'. Uniqueness: the client holds one micro market agreement, the suspended Smart Store at the Detroit plant the caller describes, so one row and one reference come back.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.invoice_reference: Value: INV-MK-451702. Basis: the tool schema says 'the settlement invoice the charge is placed on, written as INV-MK- followed by 6 digits exactly as it is printed on the invoice'. Uniqueness: find_market_ledger returns four invoices, and only INV-MK-451702 is still open - the other three each carry a payment for their exact total of 2855.00 - and it is the only one raised after the closure began.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.service_period: Value: 2026-08. Basis: the tool schema says 'the settlement period the charge covers, written as YYYY-MM with no other text'. Uniqueness: the only other row already on INV-MK-451702 carries the settlement period 2026-08.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.standby_settlement_usd: Value: 2633.70. The market has stood shut since 2026-08-14, 39 calendar days to 2026-09-22, at or beyond the 10-day minimum suspension printed against Smart Store Micro Market, and 2 suspension requests stand approved over the trailing year, at or above the repeat closure count of 2, so the closed days are divided by thirty and rounded up to 2 months. The standing charge for a month is the prompt relief share of the printed 940.00, that is 883.60, because the client settled 3 market settlement invoices over the trailing year, at or above the prompt settlement count of 3, and the 907.50 standing unsettled is below the 6500.00 minimum funding lot: 2 months give 1767.20. The management fee is charged at the pooled share of 40 percent, because the client's cafe contract at the site stands active and its ledger shows 16,070.00 of client subsidy met over the trailing year, at or above the cafe pooled floor of 15,000: 2 months of the printed 980.00 fee at 40 percent is 784.00. Half the 165.00 call-out charge, 82.50, is added for the planogram work held over the closure, because 2 planogram changes stand approved over the trailing year, at or above the planogram floor of 2, and a resumption request stands approved over the same year. The three add to 2633.70.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden write that hands back the balance left in a funding lot that has run out of time.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it changes nothing in the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Credit the client with the balance left unspent in the funding lots that have run past their drawable life, against the open settlement invoice.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: market_ext_lapsed_lot_settlement_credit is the only policy that computes lapsed_lot_credit_usd, and the lot the client pays in waits on this credit standing on the agreement.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.market_agreement_id: Value: the micro market agreement row id returned by find_market_agreements. Basis: the tool schema says 'the reference number identifying the micro market agreement being credited'. Uniqueness: one agreement is held, so one reference comes back.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.invoice_reference: Value: INV-MK-451702. Basis: the tool schema says 'the settlement invoice the credit is set against, written as INV-MK- followed by 6 digits exactly as it is printed on the invoice'. Uniqueness: it is the only settlement invoice on the ledger still carrying unsettled charges, and the credit is set against the settlement of the period it is allowed in.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.service_period: Value: 2026-08. Basis: the tool schema says 'the settlement period the credit is allowed in, written as YYYY-MM with no other text'. Uniqueness: every other row on INV-MK-451702 carries 2026-08.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.lapsed_lot_credit_usd: Value: 1249.22. A Smart Store lot stays drawable for the 12 months printed against the format, so the lapsed funding is what was paid in before the twelve months to 2026-09-22: 27,000.00 paid in all told less the 14,000.00 paid in inside those twelve months, that is 13,000.00, being the lots cleared 2025-03-12 and 2025-06-18. 26 drawdown postings stand against the agreement, at or above the busy-kiosk posting count of 8, and 20,220.00 has been drawn in all against 7,800.00 inside the twelve months, so only the 12,420.00 drawn before them is set against the lapsed funding, leaving 580.00 unspent. That is handed back at the full credit share of 100 percent, because 4 lots have been funded and 3 market settlement invoices settled over the trailing year, at or above the prompt settlement count of 3. The 165.00 call-out charge is credited twice over as closure relief, 330.00, because a suspension request stands approved over the trailing year and 5 kiosk outage requests stand approved over the same year, at or above the material outage count of 4. The high lapse share of 6 percent of the settlement is credited as well - 1 resumption request and 2 approved planogram changes stand over the trailing year - and the settlement, read over the two months to 2026-09-22 because 4 settlement charges stand there and the format is invoiced on the 18th, is 1875.00 plus 980.00 plus 165.00 plus the 2633.70 standing charge just raised, that is 5653.70, of which 6 percent is 339.22. 580.00 plus 330.00 plus 339.22 is 1249.22, below the 1413.42 period ceiling.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the customer's own funding write and hand it to her, so she can pay the lot in herself.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair for a write only the client may make; it changes nothing in the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The client pays in the subsidy funding lot the desk has sized, by bank transfer, so the kiosk discount is funded for the cover period once the market reopens.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: market_ext_subsidy_funding_lot is the only policy that computes funding_amount_usd, and the caller asked to move the money herself rather than have the desk take it.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.market_agreement_id: Value: the micro market agreement row id returned by find_market_agreements. Basis: the tool schema says 'the reference number identifying the micro market agreement being funded'. Uniqueness: one agreement is held, so one reference comes back.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.service_period: Value: 2026-09. Basis: the tool schema says 'the settlement period the lot is opened against, written as YYYY-MM with no other text'. Uniqueness: a lot is opened against the period in which it clears, and frozen_time is 2026-09-22, so it is September 2026.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_channel: Value: ach. Basis: the tool schema says 'ach where the client sends it by bank transfer out of their own accounts payable run'. Uniqueness: the caller says she will 'do it by bank transfer the moment she is told the amount', which is exactly the ach situation; check is a paper cheque, corporate_card a company card, internal_transfer money moving inside a centrally billed group and not_applicable a posting where no money moved - none of which she describes, and the three settlement payments already on her ledger are all ach.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.funding_amount_usd: Value: 19462.41. The cover runs to the whole 12-month drawable life of Smart Store Micro Market, because that life is at or beyond the long drawable life of 12 and 4 funding lots stand on the agreement, at or above the repeat funding count of 2. The take-up share is the light 18 percent, because 10 drawdown postings stand over the trailing year, at or above the busy-year posting count of 6, and a suspension request stands approved over the same year: 480 badged staff at 20.00 a month at 18 percent is 1728.00 a month. The contingency is the low 5 percent, because a suspension request and a shrink adjustment both stand over the trailing year, and it is applied once to the whole cover need: 1728.00 for 12 months raised by 5 percent is 21,772.80. Half the funding still drawable is set against it, because 4 lots stand on the agreement and a suspension request stands approved over the year: 14,000.00 funded inside the twelve months less 7,800.00 drawn inside them less the 1249.22 just handed back leaves 4950.78, half of which is 2475.39. The 165.00 call-out charge is added as the handling step, because 10 postings stand over the year and the format carries 380 distinct products, at or above the wide-range product count of 250. 21,772.80 less 2475.39 plus 165.00 is 19,462.41, above the 6500.00 minimum lot.

edges.condition: the market ledger carries a monthly settlement charge raised for the period the market stood shut on the agreement
edges.policy_source: The credit handed back for a lapsed funding lot is fixed only after the monthly settlement charge for the period the market stood shut stands on the agreement.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The agreement has stood shut since 2026-08-14, 39 calendar days to frozen_time, and no monthly settlement charge has been raised for any part of the closure: the last one on the ledger is the July management line raised 2026-08-18 for the period 2026-07, and the only row on the open invoice is a restocking charge, which is not a monthly settlement charge at all.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: raising the standing charge puts a monthly settlement charge of 2633.70 on INV-MK-451702, and the settlement read over the two-month window rises from 3020.00 to 5653.70

edges.condition: the market ledger carries a service credit on the agreement that names no kiosk, handing back the funding that has run past the months it stays drawable
edges.policy_source: The lot the client pays in is not fixed before a service credit naming no kiosk stands on the agreement, being the funding handed back to the client on a settlement.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: No service credit of any kind stands on this agreement's ledger at frozen_time, so nothing has been handed back out of the 13000.00 of funding that ran past the twelve months a Smart Store lot stays drawable - the lots cleared 2025-03-12 and 2025-06-18.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: allowing the credit puts a 1249.22 service credit on the agreement carrying no kiosk, and the funding still drawable falls from 6200.00 to 4950.78

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain, not a fan: the credit waits on the standing charge and the lot waits on the credit, so the three writes admit exactly one linear order, market_ext_standby_period_settlement then market_ext_lapsed_lot_settlement_credit then market_ext_subsidy_funding_lot. No two problems are parallel, so there is no pair of writes to reorder and no second terminal state to compare.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the standing charge and replaying everything else leaves the lapsed funding credit at 755.00 instead of 1249.22: the settlement it is measured against falls from 5653.70 to 3020.00, the lapse share falls with it and the period ceiling drops to 755.00 and bites.
Skipping the lapsed funding credit leaves the funding lot at 18837.80 instead of 19462.41, because the funding still drawable stays at 6200.00 rather than falling to 4950.78.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never names market_ext_standby_period_settlement or market_ext_lapsed_lot_settlement_credit, nor the business acts they perform. Harriet asks only to pay in the next lot of subsidy money; she never mentions a standing charge for the closure, a funding lot that has run out of time, a credit she is owed, or an unraised settlement, and she drops no hint such as 'is there anything outstanding'. Her only contribution about the prerequisites is the passive line that if the agent tells her there is something to be put straight on the account before the lot can be sized she says of course, go ahead - a reaction to something the agent has already said.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: In task_tools.py post_market_standby_settlement_ab27821d, issue_lapsed_funding_credit_131d77d2 and fund_market_subsidy_lot_f6d53aaa each compute a row id with ctx.make_id, read the parent agreement for its client and kiosk labels and its running balance, perform one ctx.create and one ctx.update carrying that posting's account delta, and return a confirmation line. None looks for a preceding charge or credit, none branches on one, none raises and none returns an error: a funding lot paid in before the credit was ever allowed is written faithfully at whatever figure it is given, and the only consequence is a different terminal hash.
